title: Decide whether the client should show the candidate
description: A candidate must pass confidence, freshness, prefix, safety, and language checks. Compare a production policy with tempting shortcuts.

scenarios.label: Routine confirmation
scenarios.draft: Thanks for moving the meeting. I'll
scenarios.candidate: send the revised agenda before noon.
scenarios.explanation: The candidate is timely, matches the active draft, and contains no blocked content.

scenarios.label: User typed ahead
scenarios.draft: Thanks for moving the meeting. I already
scenarios.candidate: sent the revised agenda before noon.
scenarios.explanation: The model is confident, but the draft changed while the request was in flight.

scenarios.label: Sensitive content
scenarios.explanation: Confidence cannot override a policy that blocks credential-like content.

scenarios.label: Language switched
scenarios.explanation: The continuation is plausible but does not follow the language at the cursor.

scenarios.label: Weak candidate
scenarios.explanation: The request is healthy, but the candidate is not strong enough to interrupt the user's attention.

policies.label: Production gate
policies.detail: Checks every release condition before rendering.

policies.label: Latency-only shortcut
policies.detail: Checks confidence and age, but ignores semantic release risks.

policies.label: Coverage-first shortcut
policies.detail: Allows older candidates and omits safety and language gates.
